findings.passage: My intention to do with this legislation is to provide teeth to Missouri's preemption law, to make sure our gun laws are consistent all across the state.
findings.note: Quoted in a news story (Missouri News Network, via the News Tribune) on his testimony at the Senate committee hearing for SB 908. He describes the bill's aim as enforcing the state's ban on local gun rules so gun laws match statewide.
subjects: one gun law for the whole state

findings.passage: When you have a jurisdiction where crime is a significant factor ... the answer to that is not to infringe upon the rights of law-abiding citizens in that jurisdiction,
findings.note: Quoted in the same news story, answering a senator's question at the SB 908 hearing about whether a city or county should have a say in protecting its citizens. He says high crime is not a reason to limit law-abiding gun owners' rights.

findings.passage: SB 908 – Deals with firearms policy, giving teeth to Missouri’s preemption law and lowering the concealed carry age from 19 to 18. This received a hearing in the Transportation, Infrastructure and Public Safety Committee this week, and will most likely become part of a larger firearms policy bill.
findings.note: From his weekly Capitol report column, published in a local paper (page date is the posting date). He summarizes his SB 908: stronger state rule over local gun laws and a lower concealed carry permit age.

News report on his SB 908: removes the current exception letting local governments regulate carry, lets a gun owner sue a local government, and sets a $50,000 payment per occurrence; the News Tribune story adds it lowers the concealed carry permit age from 19 to 18. Sponsorship itself is already on file; this adds the bill's content. A similar 2025 bill did not reach a full Senate vote.

Official Senate page: he presented SB 74, a bill modifying firearms provisions, to the Transportation, Infrastructure and Public Safety Committee. A St. Louis Public Radio story (https://www.stlpr.org/government-politics-issues/2025-02-11/missouri-senators-consider-removing-several-firearm-restrictions) describes it as barring cities and counties from setting their own open carry restrictions. The 2026 News Tribune story says it did not reach the Senate floor.
